tasks.old_behavior: The asyncio REPL checked `sys.flags.isolated` before reading PYTHONSTARTUP. The `-E` flag alone (ignore environment) did NOT suppress PYTHONSTARTUP in the asyncio REPL; only `-I` (isolated mode, which implies `-E`) did. This was inconsistent with the standard Python REPL which suppresses PYTHONSTARTUP under both `-E` and `-I`.
tasks.new_behavior: The asyncio REPL now checks `sys.flags.ignore_environment`, which is True under both `-E` and `-I`. PYTHONSTARTUP is now suppressed when either `-E` or `-I` is passed, matching the standard Python REPL behavior.
tasks.compatibility_reason: Users or scripts that rely on PYTHONSTARTUP being executed in the asyncio REPL when using only `-E` (not `-I`) will observe a behavior change: their startup file will no longer be sourced. This changes the observable CLI behavior of `python -E -m asyncio`.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test `python -E -m asyncio` with PYTHONSTARTUP set and verify the startup file is NOT sourced. Test `python -I -m asyncio` similarly. Test `python -m asyncio` without flags to ensure PYTHONSTARTUP is still sourced normally.

tasks.old_behavior: The asyncio REPL checked the PYTHON_BASIC_REPL environment variable unconditionally, regardless of `-E` or `-I` flags. If PYTHON_BASIC_REPL was set, pyrepl was disabled even when `-E` was used.
tasks.new_behavior: The asyncio REPL now checks `sys.flags.ignore_environment` before reading PYTHON_BASIC_REPL. When `-E` or `-I` is used, PYTHON_BASIC_REPL is ignored, and pyrepl availability is determined solely by the import check.
tasks.compatibility_reason: Users or scripts that set PYTHON_BASIC_REPL and use `-E` will observe different behavior: pyrepl will no longer be disabled, potentially changing the interactive experience. The asyncio REPL CLI behavior now differs when `-E` is used with PYTHON_BASIC_REPL set.
tasks.test_recommendation: Test `PYTHON_BASIC_REPL=1 python -E -m asyncio` and verify that pyrepl is NOT disabled. Test without `-E` to confirm PYTHON_BASIC_REPL still disables pyrepl.
